test_title: PYST 3: SSC CGL Tier - II (Quant) (Held On: 3 Feb 2022)
subject: maths
question: A vessel contained a solution of acid and water, in which water was 64%. Four litres of the solution was taken out of the vessel and the same quantity of water was added. If the resulting solution contains 30% acid, the quantity (in litres) of the water in the solution, at the beginning in the vessel, was:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial Acid % = 100% − 64% = 36% | Final Acid % = 30%

Ratio of Acid concentrations = 36 : 30 = 6 : 5

Since total volume remains constant after replacement, Volume ratio = 5 : 6 (Inverse of concentration)

Difference (6 − 5) = 1 unit → 4 litres replacement

Total volume (6 units) = 6 × 4 = 24 litres

Initial water = 64% of 24 = 15.36 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 15.36 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial water % = 64%

Quantity replaced = 4 litres

Final acid % = 30%

**Formula Used:**

Final Concentration = Initial Concentration × [1 − (Replaced Quantity ÷ Total Volume)]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9bbe95c8d313c695960823ce32cacb95b3063d4cf7e56907e31f6eb63b286431.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Acid % = 100% − 64% = 36%

⇒ Let Total Volume be V litres.

⇒ Acid concentration after removing 4 litres = 36%

⇒ Quantity of acid in (V − 4) litres = Final quantity of acid in V litres

⇒ 36% of (V − 4) = 30% of V

⇒ 36 × (V − 4) = 30 × V

⇒ 36V − 144 = 30V

⇒ 6V = 144

⇒ V = 144 ÷ 6 = 24 litres

⇒ Initial water = 64% of 24

⇒ Initial water = (64 ÷ 100) × 24

⇒ Initial water = 0.64 × 24 = 15.36 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 15.36 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mixture Replacement Formula

When x litres are removed from V litres and replaced by another component: Cfᵢₙₐₗ = Cᵢₙᵢₜᵢₐₗ × (1 − x/V)ⁿ, where n is the number of operations.

Alligation Method

Can be used by taking concentration of the added component (e.g., if water is added to acid-water, water concentration in added part is 100%).

Conservation of Solute

In problems where only one component is replaced/added, the quantity of the other component in the remaining mixture equals its quantity in the final mixture.</p
